newsitem.title: UK: Redland climbs after analyst's meeting.
newsitem.headline: Redland climbs after analyst's meeting.

text.p: Shares in Redland Plc climbed on Friday after an analysts' meeting the previous day spurred several analysts to adopt a more positive stance on the stock, dealers said.
Panmure Gordon analyst Robin Hardy said he had upgraded his recommendation to "buy" in the light of the meeting and dealers said NatWest Securities, BZW and HSBC James Capel were also more positive.
By 1543 GMT, Redland shares were 8-1/2p firmer at 342-1/2 on volume of 3.7 million.
Hardy said he thought a break-up and de-listing of Redland was likely and this would realise around 400p a share for investors.

"We think the group is ripe to be broken up," he said. "We already knew they were likely to sell their French business and there's a good chance they might sell their UK operations also. After that they could start selling other assets and be left with just the pan-European roofing business."
He said it would not be feasible to list this business in Britain and it would probably be listed in Frankfurt instead.

"This would leave shareholders with cash, or shares in a different company," Hardy said. "Redland Plc would cease to exist and shareholders should realise a break-up valuation of around 400p a share."
The process could happen this year, Hardy said. "I think the French business will be sold quite soon, and everything else could happen quite quickly after that."
Hardy said he now rated the stock a "buy". He said Panmure's last published recommendation was a "sell" although it had moved to "hold" at the start of this week.
Market sources said NatWest Securities had also been more positive after the analysts' meeting.
"NatWest has been tipping the share as a recovery play. There is also some talk around it could be a bid target," the head of trading at a large investment bank said.
